sentences.text: This is a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act regarding injury sustained by petitioner Ms.Indu Chaudhary d/o Sh.Momraj Chaudhary in a roadside accident occurred on 13.02.2020.

As per the averments in the claim petition, it is stated that on 13.02.2020 injured/
petitioner Indu Chaudhary was waiting for auto rickshaw at NH-24, Taj Express Tiraha, Tigri Gol Chakkar, Akbarpur, Behrampur, Vijay Nagar, Ghaziabad, UP and at about 4.45 p.m. suddenly offending vehicle bearing registration no.HR-55R-2959 (dumper) came in a high speed being driven by respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner and crushed the right foot and ankle of the petitioner.

It is stated that passersby caught hold of respondent no.1 along with offending vehicle,
someone called the police and got the injured admitted in SJM Super Specialilty Hospital, Chhijarsi,
Noida, UP.

It is stated that at the time of accident petitioner was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

2. Written statement is filed by respondent no.1 wherein an objection has been taken that no accident took place as alleged and vehicle of respondent no.2 has been falsely implicated by the police of PS Vijay Nagar.

It is denied that petitioner sustained injuries due to said accident caused by respondent no.1.
3.

Behrampur, Vijay Nagar, Ghaziabad, UP within the jurisdiction of PS Vijay Nagar due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing No.HR 55R 2959 being driven by respondent no.1/ driver?

sentences.text: It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken MACT No.293/2020 SHAILENDER MALIK Page 3 MALIK Date: 2024.04.12 16:52:42 +0530 while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

10. Petitioner/injured (PW1) has appeared in the witness box and stated that on on 13.02.2020 she was waiting for auto rickshaw at NH-24, Taj Highway Tiraha, Near Tigri Gol Chakkar, Akbarpur,
Behrampur, Vijay Nagar, Ghaziabad, UP and at about 4.45 p.m. suddenly offending vehicle bearing registration no.HR-55R-2959 (dumper) being driven by respondent no.1 rashly and negligently and in high speed came and crushed right foot and ankle of the injured.
PW1 stated that she cried with pain and passersby caught hold of respondent no.1/driver along with offending vehicle.

11. Though PW1/petitioner was cross-examined on behalf of respondents, however nothing substantive came in her cross examination regarding the manner in which accident taken place and involvement of offending vehicle no.HR-55R-2959 in the accident in question.

Moreover testimony of PW1 has been duly corroborated from police documents i.e. FIR Ex.PW1/1 and criminal case documents Ex.PW1/6 (colly.) i.e. site plan of the place of accident, release order of offending vehicle etc.

12. Driver of the offending vehicle has not appeared in the witness box to rebut the claim of the petitioner that accident was caused due to his rash and negligent driving while driving offending vehicle no.HR-55R- 2959.

As such there is sufficient material on record to establish that MACT No.293/2020 Digitally signed by Page 4 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:

Accordingly issue stands decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 13.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. 1995 AIR 755.

The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and Indu Chaudhary vs Siyaram And Ors on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87832321/
3 special damages.

sentences.text: Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
14. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

The relevant paras of the MACT No.293/2020 Digitally signed by Page 5 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.12 16:52:58 +0530 judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
Indu Chaudhary vs Siyaram And Ors on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87832321/
4 (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
 (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects  of marriage)
MACT No.293/2020 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER Page 6  MALIK Date: 2024.04.12  16:53:05 +0530  (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of  normal longevity).

sentences.text:
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i),
(ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
15.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses:

16. PW1/petitioner in her deposition stated that in the accident in question her right foot and ankle were crushed and immediately after the accident she was taken to SJM Super Speciality Hospital,
Chhijarsi, Noida UP where she was given treatment and fracture on her right foot.

PW1 stated that she spent Rs.15 lakhs on her treatment and spent more than Rs.5 lakhs in additional to Rs.15 lakhs.

18. It is matter of record that petitioner/injured was medically examined in GTB Hospital for assessing her permanent disability and as per disability certificate Ex.PW3/A petitioner received permanent locomotor impairment to the extent of 31%.
19.
As per the medical bills proved on record vide documents Ex.PW1/11 and Ex.PW2/5, a total sum of Rs.6,15,884/- has been spent by the petitioner on her medical expenses.
Therefore taking into consideration the medical treatment record, bills/invoices, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.6,15,884/- under the head of medical expenses.

Loss of earning during treatment:
20.

Petitioner/injured (PW1) in her affidavit deposed that she is a practicing Advocate was earning Rs.25,000/- per month at the time of accident and her income would have been increased by passage of time and due to experience her income would have been increased to Rs.1,00,000/- per month as on today.
Petitioner has proved her identity card issued by Shahdara Bar Association as Ex.PW1/7.
However petitioner in her cross examination admitted that she has no documentary evidence of her income being Rs.25,000/- per month as stated by her.
In such circumstances in the absence of any income proof like income tax record, passbook of bank account etc., this Tribunal would have to take the notional income of the petitioner.
Since petitioner has been a law graduate and practicing as a lawyer, her notional income would be taken at parity with minimum wages MACT No.293/2020 SHAILENDER Page 8

SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.12 16:53:21 +0530 of Delhi of a person with graduation degree, at the time of accident which is Rs.19,572/- per month.
21.

Even if the ratio of Apex Court as laid down in Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Deo Pataudi 2009 (8 ) Scale 194, is also taken into consideration wherein it was held that minimum wages are to taken into consideration in case of death of of illiterate person, where a person is having professional or technical qualification, Tribunal should take higher amount of income considering the earning capacity of the deceased/injured.

sentences.text: That judgment has been relied upon in many other judgments of Hon'ble High Courts but when the question of compensation is to be decided to be just and fair, more on the basis of logics and rationals and less on the basis of arbitrary discretion, therefore this Tribunal is of considered view when Government has already fixed minimum wages even in case of a person possessing graduate degree, such amount must be taken into consideration as notional income of the injured/deceased.

Petitioner has also stated that she was operated thrice and got treatment from SJM Super Speciality Hospital and Fortis Hospital.

Loss of future earning due to disability :
23.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
"9.
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.

If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent MACT No.293/2020 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER Page 10 MALIK Date: 2024.04.12 16:53:37 +0530 disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
10.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite Indu Chaudhary vs Siyaram And Ors on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87832321/
7 of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).

entities.text: Indu Chaudhary vs Siyaram And Ors on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."

....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.

13. We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
MACT No.293/2020
SHAILENDER  MALIK Date: 2024.04.12  16:53:45 +0530  (ii).
The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).
(iii).
The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv). The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
24.

Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra) has laid down that Tribunal is bound to assess the evidence on the record, for the purpose of ascertaining the functional disability of the petitioner on account of medical permanent disability to assess how much the medical disability adversely affected on the functional capacity of the petitioner/injured so that just and fair amount of compensation can be ascertained under the heading of future loss of earning.

sentences.text: Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, in the evidence of PW1 he has given all the details of treatment taken at different hospitals as well as about the nature of injuries suffered by her.

Beside this it has also come on the record that petitioner suffered permanent disability to the extent of 31%, permanent disability certificate is Ex.PW1/10 (Ex.PW3/A) MACT No.293/2020 by SHAILENDER Page 12 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.12 16:53:54 +0530 with regard to accidental injuries.

26. It is submitted by the counsel for the insurance that disability certificate Ex.PW3/A is not permanent in nature because as per the disability certificate patient was required to be re-assessed by medical board, after period of two years.

27. Such submission of ld. counsel for insurance however is not sustainable in view of the evidence of PW3 Dr.Udit Kumar, who was one of the member of the medical board which issued disability certificate Ex.PW3/A.

This Tribunal specifically asked a question on this aspect, in response thereto PW3 simply stated that recommendation for reassessment after two years was only for seeing the improvement if any by physiotherapy treatment, however PW3 has admitted in his evidence that even after two years the permanent disability can still remain upto 31%.
In such circumstances mere recommendation for reassessment, does not mean that permanent disability of 31% cannot be taken into consideration at all.

In view of the evidence of PW3 such reassessment was prescribed only for ensuring physiotherapy treatment but the question of permanent disability is to be decided along with functional disability of the petitioner, in the light of legal proposition as discussed above.

For the time being if there may not be any permanent disability, Tribunal still for the purpose of deciding just and fair compensation has to take into consideration all the medical evidence also to consider the functional disability of the petitioner.

In other words it is to be still seen as to what extent the accidental injuries had adversely affected functioning of the petitioner given the nature of the job, work etc.
28.
It has also come on record that petitioner has been a practicing lawyer.

Petitioner being a woman and a practicing lawyer not only suffered MACT No.293/2020 SHAILENDER Page 13 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.12 16:54:01 +0530 permanent disability but also suffered disformity to her right leg.
Being a lawyer in the district courts petitioner must require to move from one court complex to another and in that sense the disability suffered by her.

As such given the nature of the work of petitioner being a lawyer, nature of injuries suffered by her and permanent disability suffered, this Tribunal finds that petitioner had 50% functional disability.
29. Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].

(Rs.7,829/-), total Rs.27,401/-.

Thus applying the functional disability to be 50% of Rs.27,401/-,
amount comes out to be MACT No.293/2020 SHAILENDER Page 14 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK
As such the loss of future income due to disability comes out to be Rs.13,701 X 12 X 17 = Rs.27,95,004/-.

Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
31.
Petitioner in her evidence has testified that she has already spent huge amount on her medical treatment, medicines and other heads.

It is submitted by ld. counsel for petitioner that due to accidental injuries petitioner is not recovered fully yet and she has to take continuous medical treatment from different doctors and for said purpose she has to incur expenditure on conveyance apart from spending on taking special diet for speedy recovery.

Though petitioner has proved on record his medical treatment documents, but no documentary evidence in the form of prescription of doctor or bills of transportation and special diet has been placed on record to substantiate her claim that she has incurred any special amount towards conveyance and special diet.

In the absence of any such documentary proof, this Tribunal while taking into consideration period of hospitalization of petitioner, seriousness of injuries and the extent of permanent disability suffered by her, finds it appropriate to grant compensation for a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards conveyance charges and a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards special diet.

Attendant Charges:
32. Petitioner in her affidavit deposed that she has suffered great pain, mental agony, disfigurement,
loss of marriage prospects and besides that she had to pay a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month to the attendant for two years who attender her during her treatment for the injuries sustained by her in the accident.
However fact remains that no evidence has been placed on record to substantiate such claim.
Even no documentary evidence has been placed on record in support of same.

Nor any witness has been MACT No.293/2020 SHAILENDER Page 15 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.04.12 16:54:16 +0530 examined by the petitioner to the effect that services of any attendant were engaged by her.
However this Tribunal while assessing loss of income of petitioner due to accidental injuries, assessed loss of such income for one year.
Therefore it would be in the interest of justice to grant attendant charges i.e. Rs.1,20,000/- (Rs.10,000/- X 12 months).

sentences.text:
While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."

Treatment record of petitioner medical disability certificate shows she sustained medical permanent disability in relation to right leg and took treatment from different hospitals including SJM Super Speciality Hospital, Fortis Hospital etc.

Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered pain and suffering during her treatment and therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain,
sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as MACT No.293/2020 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.12 16:54:24 +0530 consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
Accordingly, Rs.1,50,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.

35.

Therefore taking into consideration nature of injuries, disability, he is awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.

It is apparent not only from the photographs of the petitioner, but also medical treatment record that petitioner has not only suffered physical disability but also suffered disformity of her right leg.

Being a lawyer in district courts of Delhi, petitioner is required to move from one court complex to another and in that sense disability suffered by her must have caused not only case of disability but a case of disformity and therefore she is also required to be compensated on that account.
As such this Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) Whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) If the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement;
(iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.
As such there is sufficient material on record to establish that MACT No.293/2020 Digitally signed by Page 4 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.04.12 16:52:51 +0530 accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no.HR-55R-2959.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. 1995 AIR 755.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
Even if the ratio of Apex Court as laid down in Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Deo Pataudi 2009 (8 ) Scale 194, is also taken into consideration wherein it was held that minimum wages are to taken into consideration in case of death of of illiterate person, where a person is having professional or technical qualification, Tribunal should take higher amount of income considering the earning capacity of the deceased/injured.
That judgment has been relied upon in many other judgments of Hon'ble High Courts but when the question of compensation is to be decided to be just and fair, more on the basis of logics and rationals and less on the basis of arbitrary discretion, therefore this Tribunal is of considered view when Government has already fixed minimum wages even in case of a person possessing graduate degree, such amount must be taken into consideration as notional income of the injured/deceased.
Therefore this Tribunal considering the nature of injuries, treatment given, petitioner is entitled for loss of income due to treatment for period of one year since the day of accident.
In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.
The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.
To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).
The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.
In such circumstances mere recommendation for reassessment, does not mean that permanent disability of 31% cannot be taken into consideration at all.
In view of the evidence of PW3 such reassessment was prescribed only for ensuring physiotherapy treatment but the question of permanent disability is to be decided along with functional disability of the petitioner, in the light of legal proposition as discussed above.
For the time being if there may not be any permanent disability, Tribunal still for the purpose of deciding just and fair compensation has to take into consideration all the medical evidence also to consider the functional disability of the petitioner.
In other words it is to be still seen as to what extent the accidental injuries had adversely affected functioning of the petitioner given the nature of the job, work etc.
